model.name: Alias / Same-as Mapping
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral mixin that lets any subject model carry federated identity-equivalence assertions between identifiers or records held in different systems, each qualified by who asserted it, on what authority, by what method, with what confidence and on what evidence.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-036 governs the assertion that two or more identifiers, records or resource references denote the same real-world subject, together with everything needed to interpret, reproduce, dispute and supersede that assertion. It covers the equivalence assertion itself and its relation predicate and strength; the actors, authorities and source systems standing behind it; the matching or curation method reference, its configuration, features and thresholds; the score, calibration and uncertainty attached to it; the positive, negative and contradictory evidence cited for it; review and adjudication outcomes; and the states of agreement, dispute and undetermined. It deliberately keeps confidence, formal relation semantics and authority as three independent axes so that a high score never silently becomes identity and an authoritative assertion never silently becomes statistical certainty. It is storage- and interface-neutral: JSON, YAML, Markdown, RDF, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of the same semantics.
in_scope: Equivalence assertions between two or more identifiers, records or resource references, including negative (explicitly-not-the-same) and undetermined assertions
The formal relation predicate asserted and its declared semantic strength, and the constraints on projecting it onto transitive or substitution-licensing predicates
Attribution of the assertion to a claimant or asserter, a responsible authority, a publisher, a reviewer of record and an approving actor, kept as distinct roles
Source-system binding for each side of the assertion, including the authoritative master-system record reference where one exists, and derivation from prior assertions
Creation, observation, ingestion, decision and validity times of the assertion, recorded separately when they differ

Reference to the match, curation or reasoning method, its tool and version, configuration digest, exact rules, normalization, comparison functions and blocking keys, sufficient for an independent party to reproduce the decision
Score, score scale, decision thresholds, decision region, uncertainty, calibration statement and per-feature explanation reported by the referenced method
Evaluation results attached to the method: gold-standard reference, false-positive and false-negative rates, precision and recall, disaggregated subgroup performance and declared cost asymmetry
Evidence items cited for or against the assertion, with citation, digest, strength, sensitivity classification, jurisdiction of origin, freshness and retraction status
Human review, adjudication outcome and reason, and the automated-versus-manual origin marker
Competing assertions between authorities, non-destructive confidence revision and the explicit undetermined or no-decision state
out_of_scope: Execution of matching, blocking, scoring or clustering: the matching or entity-resolution engine is referenced, never embedded, and this model owns no execution semantics
Training, tuning, drift monitoring or lifecycle of machine-learning models used by a referenced matcher
Minting, allocation, formatting or validation of the underlying identifiers, which belong to the parent identifier and identity model
Master-data merge, survivorship, golden-record construction and downstream record consolidation
Definition of the real-world subjects being equated, their attributes and their own lifecycles
Runtime evaluation, enforcement or refusal of access, consent and data-sharing policy, which belongs to the adopting Dimension's policy model
Storage and semantics of the audit trail or event log; this model cites audit records but does not own audit-trail semantics
Execution of deletion and disposition, which is performed under the adopting Dimension's retention policy
Cryptanalytic risk assessment of privacy-preserving encodings such as Bloom-filter identifiers
Statistical disclosure control and release approval for datasets derived from linked data

boundary_notes.distinction: The parent owns what an identifier is, who issues it, its syntax and its validity. WM-XCT-036 owns only the assertion that two such identifiers denote the same subject, and never redefines or re-validates the identifiers themselves.

The engine performs blocking, comparison and scoring. This model carries the method reference, configuration digest, feature inventory, thresholds and reported score as recorded parameters and outcomes; it does not execute, schedule or optimise them, and holding a score confers no ownership of the scoring process.

PROV supplies the agent, activity, attribution, derivation and bundle vocabulary that this model aligns to. This model does not redefine provenance semantics; it binds subject-specific provenance roles to PROV terms. PROV has no confidence construct, so confidence is carried separately.

Formal meaning of exactMatch, closeMatch and SameIndividual, including transitivity and substitution licensing, is owned by those specifications. This model records which predicate is asserted and constrains projection onto them; it does not restate or vary their entailment rules.

Quality metrics, dimensions and measurement structure follow DQV. This model references measurements and evaluation runs about a method or mapping set; it does not define metric catalogues or run quality assessments.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Access-control, consent and retention policy model of the adopting Dimension
boundary_notes.distinction: This model classifies evidence sensitivity and records jurisdiction of origin so that a policy model can decide. Evaluation of those policies, enforcement of access decisions and execution of deletion are performed elsewhere.

Adjudication records and confidence revisions are content of this model. The immutable audit trail that proves who read or changed them is a referenced record; this model neither stores nor defines audit-trail semantics.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Normative vocabulary for agents (Person, Organization, SoftwareAgent), attribution, qualified association and role, generation time and derivation: the backbone for separating asserter, authority, publisher, reviewer and approver on one equivalence assertion.

sources.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
sources.relevance: Defines alternateOf and specializationOf for entities that present aspects of the same thing, plus hadPrimarySource, wasRevisionOf, wasInvalidatedBy and Bundle for provenance-of-provenance: directly supports lineage, supersession and non-destructive revision of alias assertions.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Section 10 mapping properties: exactMatch is symmetric and transitive, closeMatch is deliberately non-transitive to avoid compound errors across schemes, and exactMatch is disjoint from broadMatch and relatedMatch. Sets the constraint that relation semantics are independent of match confidence.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Structural Specification and Functional-Style Syntax (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: SameIndividual and DifferentIndividuals axioms and the absence of a Unique Name Assumption: establishes that identity must be explicitly asserted, that same-as licenses full substitution, and that explicit non-identity is a first-class assertion.

sources.title: Data on the Web Best Practices: Data Quality Vocabulary
sources.relevance: QualityMeasurement, Metric, value, isMeasurementOf, computedOn, QualityAnnotation and QualityCertificate, with PROV reused for the provenance of quality assessments: the pattern for attaching calibration and evaluation results without inventing a local metric model.

sources.title: SSSOM specification: Mapping and MappingSet data model
sources.version_or_date: SSSOM specification version 1.1 (sssom_version slot introduced), accessed 2026-09-04
sources.relevance: First-party technical definition of the mapping metadata surface: mapping_justification, confidence, similarity_score and measure, mapping_tool and mapping_tool_version, author_id, creator_id, reviewer_id, mapping_date, subject_source_version, predicate_modifier, curation_rule and mapping_cardinality.

sources.title: A Simple Standard for Sharing Ontological Mappings (SSSOM)
sources.organization: Matentzoglu et al., Database (Oxford University Press)
sources.version_or_date: Submitted 13 December 2021; published in Database, doi:10.1093/database/baac035
sources.relevance: Peer-reviewed argument that mappings circulated without justification, confidence and review provenance cause incorrect assumptions and are unsafe for precision-critical use, and that curated and automated mappings cannot be reconciled without recorded method metadata.

sources.title: A Theory for Record Linkage
sources.organization: Fellegi and Sunter, Journal of the American Statistical Association
sources.relevance: Foundational decision theory for probabilistic linkage: likelihood-ratio weights from m- and u-probabilities, two thresholds, and the three-way decision link, possible link and non-link at stipulated error bounds. Normative basis for an explicit undetermined state rather than a forced binary outcome.

sources.title: Record Linkage Project Process Model
sources.relevance: Public-authority process model covering data preparation and standardization, blocking and indexing, deterministic versus probabilistic method selection, comparison functions and decision rules, threshold setting, clerical review, internal and external validation of false-positive and false-negative rates, documentation duties, and secure storage with data destruction timelines.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-63A-4, Digital Identity Guidelines: Identity Proofing and Enrollment
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Establishes that identity claims rest on graded evidence at defined identity assurance levels, and that resolution to a unique identity plus the evidence relied upon must be recorded. Anchors the separation of authority-derived assurance from statistical match confidence.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 5: Person resource and IdentityAssuranceLevel value set
sources.relevance: Person.link.target with Person.link.assurance bound to IdentityAssuranceLevel (level1 little or no confidence, level2 some confidence, level3 high confidence, level4 very high confidence): a deployed normative example of an equivalence link carrying an ordinal assurance qualifier distinct from the link itself.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative date-time profile requiring seconds and a time-offset of Z or plus/minus HH:MM, with -00:00 reserved for a known UTC time whose local offset is unknown. Governs all decision, observation and ingestion timestamps in this model.

sources.title: A guide to evaluating linkage quality for the analysis of linked data
sources.organization: Harron et al., International Journal of Epidemiology (Oxford University Press)
sources.relevance: Peer-reviewed methodology for evaluating linkage quality: gold-standard validation yielding sensitivity and positive predictive value, comparison of linked against unlinked records using standardized differences to expose subgroup bias, and sensitivity analyses across thresholds and algorithms.

bundles.name: Assertion provenance, responsibility and time
bundles.description: Everything needed to say who stands behind an alias assertion, on what authority, out of which source systems, derived from what earlier assertion, and at which distinct points in time.
bundles.rationale: PROV establishes that responsibility for an entity is expressed through attribution to typed agents with qualified roles, and that derivation and primary source are first-class. SSSOM shows that mapping consumers cannot calibrate trust without author, creator, reviewer, source version and date. A same-as claim without an attributable asserter and a resolvable source binding cannot be audited, disputed or reproduced.

layers.name: Responsible actors and authority basis
layers.description: The distinct agent roles attached to one equivalence assertion and the mandate under which an authoritative assertion is made.

findings.name: Distinct actor roles and authority mandate on one assertion
findings.description: An alias assertion carries several separable responsibilities that are routinely collapsed in practice: the claimant or asserter that states the equivalence, the responsible authority accountable for it, the publisher that releases it, the reviewer of record who inspected it and the approving actor who authorised it. Each is a reference to an agent in an external registry, typed as person, organization or software agent, and each may be absent. The finding also carries the mandate or instrument giving an authority the standing to assert equivalence and the scope of that mandate, which is what makes an assertion authoritative rather than merely confident.

questions.text: Which agent asserted this equivalence, and is that agent a person, an organization or a software agent?
answer_data: Resolvable agent reference in an external party registry
Agent type code aligned to PROV Person, Organization or SoftwareAgent
Origin marker distinguishing automated, manual and mixed assertion

questions.text: Under what mandate or instrument does the responsible authority have standing to declare these identifiers equivalent, and over what scope?
answer_data: Reference to the authority agent
Citation of the mandating instrument, register designation or delegation
Scope expression covering subject population, identifier namespaces and jurisdiction

questions.text: Who published this assertion and who remains accountable for it after publication?
answer_data: Publisher agent reference
Accountable authority reference
Publication channel or mapping-set reference

questions.text: Was the assertion approved by an actor distinct from the asserter, and what act recorded that approval?
answer_data: Approver agent reference
Reference to the approval activity or decision record
Boolean indicating separation of asserter and approver

questions.text: How is each role attributed so that a consumer can resolve the agent without ambiguity?
answer_data: Qualified attribution structure naming agent and role
Persistent agent identifier such as an organisational register key or researcher identifier
Statement of which roles were left unrecorded and why

data_elements.name: Asserter reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent that states the equivalence assertion.

data_elements.name: Asserter agent kind
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing a person, an organization and a software agent, aligned to PROV agent subtypes.

data_elements.name: Origin mode
data_elements.description: Whether the assertion originated from automated processing, manual curation, or a mixed workflow.

data_elements.name: Responsible authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent accountable for the assertion once published.

data_elements.name: Authority basis
data_elements.description: The mandate, instrument or delegation that gives the authority standing to declare equivalence.

data_elements.name: Authority scope
data_elements.description: Subject population, identifier namespaces and jurisdiction over which the mandate applies.

data_elements.name: Publisher reference
data_elements.description: Agent that released the assertion or the mapping set containing it.

data_elements.name: Approving actor reference
data_elements.description: Agent that authorised publication or operational use of the assertion.

data_elements.name: Reviewer of record reference
data_elements.description: Agent or agents who inspected the assertion and signed off, distinct from the asserter.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Actor roles are pure reference data: each role resolves to an agent held in an external party or authority registry, and the mandate is a citation rather than a document this model holds. Materialising an actor file here would duplicate the referenced registry and create a second, divergent record of agent identity.

layers.name: Source lineage and assertion time points
layers.description: The systems and prior assertions an equivalence claim came from, and the separately recorded moments at which it was observed, decided, ingested and made valid.

findings.name: Source-system binding and derivation lineage
findings.description: Each side of an equivalence assertion is bound to the source system that supplied the identifier and, where one exists, to the authoritative master-system record that governs the subject. The source version or edition matters because a mapping valid against one release of a source may be invalid against the next. The finding also records derivation from prior assertions, the primary source of a re-published claim, and the provenance container that lets provenance itself be described and attributed.

questions.text: Which source system supplied each identifier in this assertion, and which version or edition of that source was in effect?
answer_data: Source-system reference per side
Source version or edition label per side
Namespace or prefix declaration used to expand each identifier

questions.text: Does an authoritative master-system record govern either side, and how is it referenced rather than copied?
answer_data: Master-record reference with issuing-system identification
Statement that the local record dereferences rather than mirrors the master attributes
Flag where no master system exists for that side

questions.text: Was this assertion derived from an earlier assertion or re-published from another mapping set, and what is its primary source?
answer_data: References to predecessor assertions
Primary-source reference for republished claims
Revision relationship where the assertion supersedes an earlier version

questions.text: What must travel with the assertion so that lineage survives export to a different serialisation or repository?
answer_data: Provenance container or bundle reference grouping the assertion's provenance statements
Minimum portable lineage element set
Identifier expansion map required for round-tripping

data_elements.name: Subject-side source reference
data_elements.description: Source system that supplied the subject identifier of the assertion.

data_elements.name: Object-side source reference
data_elements.description: Source system that supplied the object identifier of the assertion.

data_elements.name: Source version
data_elements.description: Version or edition label of each bound source, recorded per side.

data_elements.name: Authoritative master-record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the governing record in the master system for a side, where such a system exists.

data_elements.name: Derived-from reference
data_elements.description: Prior assertion or mapping set from which this assertion was derived or revised.

data_elements.name: Provenance container reference
data_elements.description: Named container grouping the provenance statements about this assertion, itself attributable.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Lineage is a set of references and version labels pointing at systems and records owned elsewhere. Producing a lineage document here would copy master-system content into this model and create a stale second copy that competes with the authoritative record it points at.

findings.name: Separately recorded assertion time points
findings.description: Alias assertions have several genuinely different times that are routinely conflated: the moment the compared source states were observed, the moment the equivalence decision was reached, the moment the assertion entered this store, the moment the record was created, and the interval over which the equivalence is asserted to hold. Conflating them makes it impossible to tell a stale decision from a stale ingest, or to reason about an assertion that was correct when made and wrong now. All values follow RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

questions.text: When was the equivalence decision reached, and when were the source states it compared actually observed?
answer_data: Decision timestamp in RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z
Observation timestamp per side where source states were read at different moments
Statement of the clock or time authority relied on

questions.text: When did this assertion enter the current store, and how is that kept distinct from when it was decided?
answer_data: Ingestion timestamp
Record creation timestamp
Rule that ingestion time is never substituted for decision time when the two differ

questions.text: Over what interval is the equivalence asserted to hold, and what happens outside that interval?
answer_data: Validity interval start and end
Open-ended marker where no end is asserted
Behaviour for queries outside the interval, expressed as a declared assumption

questions.text: How is a timestamp with an unknown local offset represented without silently claiming UTC preference?
answer_data: Use of the -00:00 offset form for a known UTC instant with unknown local offset
Rejection rule for timestamps lacking seconds or an offset
Conformance check applied at ingestion

data_elements.name: Decision time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the equivalence decision was reached by the asserting agent or method.

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the compared source record states were read, recorded per side when they differ.

data_elements.name: Ingestion time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the assertion entered the current store.

data_elements.name: Record creation time
data_elements.description: Instant at which this alias-assertion record was created.

data_elements.name: Asserted validity interval
data_elements.description: Interval over which the equivalence is asserted to hold, with an open-ended end permitted.

data_elements.name: Time authority
data_elements.description: Clock, service or agent relied on for the recorded instants.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Time points are scalar values attached directly to the assertion record. There is no document, media object or serialised deliverable to identify separately, and creating one would fragment values that must be read atomically with the assertion.

bundles.name: Match method, score and calibrated confidence
bundles.description: The recorded specification of how an equivalence was reached and how much weight its confidence deserves, sufficient for an independent party to reproduce the decision without this model containing the matching engine.
bundles.rationale: Fellegi and Sunter define linkage as a decision rule over likelihood ratios with two thresholds and an explicit possible-link region at stipulated error bounds; Statistics Canada operationalises that into standardization, blocking, comparison rules, thresholds and quality assessment; SSSOM shows the metadata that must accompany a mapping for the decision to be interpretable. Reproduction requires the method identity, configuration, features and thresholds to be recorded as data, not inferred from a running system.

layers.name: Reproducible method specification
layers.description: Identity and version of the method that produced the assertion, and the feature, normalization and candidate-generation configuration it ran with.

findings.name: Method identity, justification category, tool version and configuration digest
findings.description: Every assertion names the method that produced it, classified by justification category such as manual curation, lexical matching, logical inference or composite matching, and identified by tool name and exact version. Where the method is a deterministic rule set, the exact rule expression or a resolvable reference to it is carried, and rules that are local heuristics rather than governed standard methods are labelled as such. A configuration digest binds the assertion to the precise parameter set used, which is what makes the decision reproducible rather than merely describable.

questions.text: Which method produced this assertion, and what tool and exact version executed it?
answer_data: Method reference resolvable to a specification
Tool name and immutable version string
Configuration digest binding the assertion to a parameter set

questions.text: What category of justification underlies the assertion: manual curation, lexical or structural matching, logical inference, or composite?
answer_data: Justification category code drawn from a governed mapping-justification vocabulary
Statement of unspecified justification where the category is genuinely unknown
Composite decomposition where several justifications combine

questions.text: For a deterministic method, what is the exact rule expression applied, and is it a governed standard method or a local heuristic?
answer_data: Rule expression text or resolvable curation-rule reference
Flag distinguishing governed method from local heuristic
Order of rule passes where a hierarchical deterministic strategy is used

questions.text: What must be recorded so an independent party can reproduce the decision without access to the original matching engine?
answer_data: Method specification artifact and its version tag
Configuration snapshot and its content digest
Explicit list of runtime dependencies referenced but not held by this model

data_elements.name: Method reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the match, curation or inference method that produced the assertion.

data_elements.name: Mapping justification code
data_elements.description: Governed category describing the kind of justification, such as manual curation, lexical matching or logical inference.

data_elements.name: Matching tool name
data_elements.description: Name of the tool or pipeline that executed the method.

data_elements.name: Matching tool version
data_elements.description: Immutable version string of the executing tool.

data_elements.name: Configuration digest
data_elements.description: Content digest of the serialized parameter set in effect for the decision.

data_elements.name: Rule expression reference
data_elements.description: Exact deterministic rule text or a resolvable curation-rule reference.

data_elements.name: Local heuristic flag
data_elements.description: Marks a rule that is a locally invented heuristic rather than a governed standard method.

artifacts.name: Match method specification
artifacts.description: The versioned human- and machine-readable description of the method: its decision logic, parameter meanings, assumptions and known limitations, referenced by every assertion the method produced.
media_or_form: versioned specification document in PDF, HTML or Markdown
artifacts.identity_strategy: Method identifier issued by the owning method registry or repository, combined with an immutable version tag; where no registry exists, a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension and permanently bound to the specification content digest.

artifacts.name: Method configuration snapshot
artifacts.description: The exact serialized parameter set, feature weights, threshold values and environment manifest used for one execution of the method, retained so a decision can be re-derived.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Content digest of the serialized configuration as the primary key, accompanied by a monotonically increasing run sequence number scoped to the method identifier; no date component is used in the identifier.

findings.name: Feature inventory, normalization, comparison functions and candidate generation
findings.description: What the method actually compared, how each field was standardised before comparison, which comparison function and parameters were applied per field, and which blocking or indexing keys generated the candidate set. Blocking is decisive because a pair never generated as a candidate can never be linked, so a missing blocking record makes false negatives uninterpretable. This finding also records whether features were held in cleartext, hashed or privacy-preserving encoded form, and which attributes were deliberately excluded and why.

questions.text: Which fields were used as comparison features, and which available fields were deliberately excluded?
answer_data: Ordered inventory of comparison fields with source path per side
Excluded-field list with a recorded reason for each exclusion
Discriminating power or agreement weight recorded per field where estimated

questions.text: What normalization or standardization was applied to each field before comparison, and in what order?
answer_data: Ordered preprocessing step list per field
Comparison function and parameters per field
Handling rule for missing and partially populated values

questions.text: How was the candidate pair set generated, and what pairs could the blocking strategy never produce?
answer_data: Blocking or indexing keys and pass order
Declared coverage limitation of the blocking strategy
Estimated recall loss attributable to blocking where measured

questions.text: Were features compared in cleartext, hashed or privacy-preserving encoded form, and what does that choice cost in interpretability?
answer_data: Feature representation code covering cleartext, hashed and encoded forms
Encoding parameter reference where a privacy-preserving representation is used
Statement of reduced explainability under encoded comparison

questions.text: What was the assessed quality of each linkage variable in the sources, and how did that constrain the method?
answer_data: Per-field completeness and discordance assessment
Note on fields whose recording quality varies across subgroups
Method adjustments made in response to poor field quality

data_elements.name: Comparison feature inventory
data_elements.description: Ordered list of fields compared, with the source path for each side.

data_elements.name: Normalization step
data_elements.description: Ordered preprocessing operation applied to a field before comparison.

data_elements.name: Comparison function
data_elements.description: Comparator and its parameters applied to a field pair, including agreement and disagreement handling.

data_elements.name: Blocking key
data_elements.description: Key or index used to generate candidate pairs, with its pass order.

data_elements.name: Feature representation
data_elements.description: Whether features were compared in cleartext, hashed or privacy-preserving encoded form.

data_elements.name: Excluded feature
data_elements.description: Attribute deliberately withheld from comparison, with the recorded reason.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The feature and normalization configuration is structured data that must be queryable per field and per assertion; it is bound by digest to the method configuration snapshot already declared under method identity. Emitting a second document here would duplicate that snapshot and risk the two diverging.

layers.name: Score, calibration and the meaning of strength
layers.description: The numeric or ordinal strength attached to an assertion, the evidence that the number means what it claims, and the rules that stop a score from being read as semantics or as authority.

findings.name: Score, scale, thresholds and decision region
findings.description: A confidence value is uninterpretable without its scale and the thresholds it was compared against. Fellegi-Sunter weights are unbounded log-likelihood ratios, SSSOM confidence is a bounded zero-to-one value and FHIR assurance is a four-point ordinal scale; these are not interchangeable. The decision region records whether the pair fell in the link, possible-link or non-link band, which preserves the possible-link outcome instead of forcing a binary answer. An explanation, such as per-field weight contributions or a rule trace, makes the outcome inspectable.

questions.text: What is the score value and on which scale is it expressed, so it is not compared against an incompatible scale?
answer_data: Score value
Scale code covering bounded probability, unbounded likelihood weight and ordinal assurance level
Scale bounds and direction where applicable

questions.text: Which upper and lower thresholds were in force, and in which decision region did the pair fall?
answer_data: Upper and lower threshold values with their scale
Decision region code covering link, possible link and non-link
Reference to the threshold-setting decision and who set it

questions.text: What per-feature contributions or rule trace explain how this score arose?
answer_data: Per-field weight or agreement contribution list
Rule trace for deterministic methods
Statement where the method is not decomposable into per-feature contributions

questions.text: What state does a pair in the possible-link band hold before any clerical review resolves it?
answer_data: Undetermined state marker distinct from rejected
Queue or escalation reference for pending resolution
Rule prohibiting silent promotion of a possible link to a link

data_elements.name: Score value
data_elements.description: Numeric strength reported by the referenced method for this pair.

data_elements.name: Score scale
data_elements.description: Scale on which the score is expressed, including its bounds and direction.

data_elements.name: Upper threshold
data_elements.description: Threshold at or above which the method declares a link.

data_elements.name: Lower threshold
data_elements.description: Threshold at or below which the method declares a non-link.

data_elements.name: Decision region
data_elements.description: Band the pair fell into: link, possible link or non-link.

data_elements.name: Score explanation
data_elements.description: Per-feature contributions or rule trace supporting the reported score.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Score, scale, thresholds and region are scalar values that must be read atomically with the assertion and compared across assertions in queries. They carry no media form of their own, and the reproducible configuration behind them is already held as the method configuration snapshot artifact.

findings.name: Calibration, evaluation results, subgroup performance and cost asymmetry
findings.description: A score deserves weight only insofar as it has been evaluated. This finding attaches evaluation evidence to the method or mapping set rather than inventing it per pair: the gold-standard or training reference used, estimated false-positive and false-negative rates with precision and recall, whether scores are calibrated probabilities or merely monotone rankings, performance disaggregated by subgroup to expose differential linkage error, and the declared relative cost of a false positive against a false negative that justifies where thresholds sit.

questions.text: Are the reported scores calibrated probabilities, or only a monotone ranking that must not be read as a probability?
answer_data: Calibration statement with the calibration method used
Reference to the calibration measurement
Explicit non-calibration declaration where none was performed

questions.text: What false-positive and false-negative rates were estimated for this method, and against what reference?
answer_data: False-positive and false-negative rate estimates with uncertainty intervals
Precision, recall or sensitivity and positive predictive value
Gold-standard or training-data reference and its representativeness caveat

questions.text: How was linkage quality evaluated where no representative gold standard was available?
answer_data: Comparison of linked against unlinked records using standardized differences
Sensitivity analysis across thresholds or alternative algorithms
External validation by confrontation with an independent source

questions.text: Does linkage error differ across identifiable subgroups, and how is that disparity reported?
answer_data: Performance metrics disaggregated by subgroup
Statement of which subgroup attributes were available for disaggregation and which were not
Declared limitation where subgroup evaluation was not possible

questions.text: What relative cost of a false positive against a false negative was assumed when the thresholds were placed?
answer_data: Declared cost asymmetry statement
Consequence description for each error type in the adopting use case
Reference to the actor who accepted the residual error rates

data_elements.name: Evaluation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an evaluation run whose results qualify this method or mapping set.

data_elements.name: Gold-standard reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the dataset of known true match status used for validation, with its representativeness caveat.

data_elements.name: Error-rate measurement
data_elements.description: Estimated false-positive and false-negative rates, precision and recall, with uncertainty intervals.

data_elements.name: Subgroup performance result
data_elements.description: Linkage-quality metrics disaggregated by subgroup to expose differential error.

data_elements.name: Calibration statement
data_elements.description: Whether scores are calibrated probabilities, and by what method, or explicitly uncalibrated.

data_elements.name: Declared cost asymmetry
data_elements.description: Stated relative cost of a false positive against a false negative for the adopting use case.

artifacts.name: Linkage quality evaluation report
artifacts.description: The report of one evaluation of a method or mapping set: reference data used, metrics obtained, disaggregated subgroup results, sensitivity analyses, limitations and the residual error accepted.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Evaluation-run identifier issued by the evaluating organisation's system of record where one exists; otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, scoped to the method identifier and the evaluation reference dataset, with no date component in the identifier.

findings.name: Separation of statistical confidence, relation semantics and authority
findings.description: Three independent axes are habitually collapsed and must be kept apart. The relation predicate carries formal semantics: an exact-match predicate is transitive and a same-individual axiom licenses full substitution, while a close-match predicate is deliberately non-transitive precisely to stop compound errors accumulating across schemes. Statistical confidence is a property of a method's output. Authority-derived assurance is a property of who asserted it. A score of 0.99 does not license substitution; an authoritative registry assertion carries no statistical error estimate; and a negative assertion of non-identity is a first-class claim rather than the absence of a positive one.

questions.text: Which formal predicate is asserted, and does that predicate license transitive closure or full substitution?
answer_data: Relation predicate identifier from a governed vocabulary
Transitivity and symmetry properties of the chosen predicate
Substitution licence flag indicating whether downstream inference may replace one identifier with the other

questions.text: How are statistical confidence, semantic strength and authority-derived assurance recorded so that none can be derived from another?
answer_data: Semantic strength code separate from the score field
Authority-derived assurance level separate from both
Rule prohibiting derivation of one axis from another

questions.text: When an authority asserts equivalence without a method, what does that imply and not imply about error probability?
answer_data: Assurance level recorded with no implied score
Explicit statement that no error estimate exists for authority-only assertions
Reference to the mandate under which the assertion was made

questions.text: How is an explicit assertion that two identifiers are not the same represented, distinctly from an unproven or absent link?
answer_data: Negation modifier applied to the predicate
Distinct different-individuals style assertion
Separation of asserted non-identity from undetermined and from unassessed

data_elements.name: Relation predicate
data_elements.description: The formal predicate asserted between the two identifiers, drawn from a governed relation vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Semantic strength
data_elements.description: Declared strength of the relation: substitutable equivalence, scheme-local close match, related, or asserted non-identity.

data_elements.name: Authority-derived assurance level
data_elements.description: Ordinal assurance in the asserted identity's accuracy derived from evidence and authority, recorded independently of any score.

data_elements.name: Substitution licence
data_elements.description: Whether downstream systems may substitute one identifier for the other in inference or query.

data_elements.name: Projection constraint
data_elements.description: Constraint on projecting this assertion onto a transitive or substitution-licensing predicate during export.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are typed classification values and constraint statements evaluated at query and export time. They exist only as attributes of the assertion, have no independent media form, and any document restating them would duplicate the governed relation vocabularies this model aligns to rather than owns.

bundles.name: Evidence, contradiction and adjudication
bundles.description: The cited evidence for and against an equivalence, its integrity and freshness, the human review that resolved it, and the handling of competing authorities and genuinely undetermined cases.
bundles.rationale: Identity proofing rests on graded evidence that must be recorded together with the resolution decision. Statistics Canada builds clerical review into the linkage process, and Fellegi-Sunter reserves an explicit possible-link outcome rather than forcing a choice. SSSOM records reviewer sign-off precisely because a tool-proposed mapping and a human-confirmed mapping warrant different trust. None of this is available if evidence is unattributed, undated or silently overwritten.

layers.name: Evidence items and their integrity over time
layers.description: What was cited for or against the equivalence, how it is identified and verified, and how its currency, retraction and absence are handled.

findings.name: Positive, negative and contradictory evidence items with citation and integrity
findings.description: Evidence is registered as discrete items rather than folded into a narrative, each with polarity (supporting, refuting or ambiguous), a resolvable citation or locator, a content digest so tampering or substitution is detectable, a graded strength, a sensitivity classification identifying special-category or restricted identifiers, and the jurisdiction the evidence originated in. Contradictory items are retained side by side; the model does not resolve them by discarding one.

questions.text: Which items support the equivalence, which refute it, and which are ambiguous?
answer_data: Evidence item references with polarity code
Retention rule keeping refuting items alongside supporting ones
Note where the same item supports one interpretation and refutes another

questions.text: How strong is each evidence item, and on what graded scale is that strength expressed?
answer_data: Graded evidence strength code with its scale definition
Basis for the grade, such as issuing authority and verification performed
Distinction between validating the evidence and verifying it belongs to the subject

questions.text: How is each cited item identified and verified so that substitution or alteration is detectable?
answer_data: Resolvable citation or locator
Content digest with the algorithm named
Digest stub retained where the item itself may not be stored

questions.text: Which cited items contain sensitive or special-category identifiers, and from which jurisdiction did they originate?
answer_data: Sensitivity classification per item
Jurisdiction of origin code
Reference to the policy model that decides permitted reuse, which this model does not evaluate

questions.text: Who may read a given evidence item, and how is the assertion still usable when an item is not readable to a consumer?
answer_data: Access classification per item referencing an external policy
Redacted projection exposing polarity and strength without content
Statement that access enforcement is performed by the referenced policy model

data_elements.name: Evidence item reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a discrete item cited in relation to the equivalence.

data_elements.name: Evidence polarity
data_elements.description: Whether an item supports, refutes or is ambiguous with respect to the equivalence.

data_elements.name: Evidence citation
data_elements.description: Resolvable citation or locator for the item as held by its owning system.

data_elements.name: Evidence digest
data_elements.description: Content digest of the item, with the algorithm named, enabling integrity verification.

data_elements.name: Evidence strength
data_elements.description: Graded strength of the item on a declared scale, with the basis for the grade.

data_elements.name: Evidence sensitivity classification
data_elements.description: Classification identifying special-category or otherwise restricted content in the item.

data_elements.name: Evidence jurisdiction of origin
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction under which the item was created or released, recorded for the policy model to evaluate.

artifacts.name: Retained evidence exhibit
artifacts.description: The retained copy, extract or verifiable digest stub of one cited evidence item, held so that a later reviewer can inspect what the original asserter actually saw.
media_or_form: digest stub where the item itself must not be retained
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative source-system identifier of the evidence document where the issuing system provides one; otherwise the content digest of the retained exhibit; a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension is used only when neither is available.

findings.name: Evidence currency, retraction and declared absence
findings.description: Evidence decays. An item that justified an equivalence three source-releases ago may since have been superseded, corrected or withdrawn by its issuer, and an equivalence may have rested on evidence that was never available at all. This finding records the instant each item speaks to, the freshness window beyond which it should not be relied on unreviewed, retraction and supersession pointers, an explicit declaration of evidence that is missing or was sought and not found, and the point at which the assertion is due for revalidation.

questions.text: What instant does each evidence item speak to, as distinct from when it was cited?
answer_data: As-of instant per item in RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z
Citation instant recorded separately
Note where the as-of instant is unknown rather than assumed

questions.text: Beyond what age should an evidence item no longer be relied on without re-checking?
answer_data: Freshness window expressed as a duration per evidence class
Revalidation due point for the assertion
Consequence of an expired window, expressed as a state change rather than an enforcement action

questions.text: How is an item recorded once its issuer has corrected, superseded or withdrawn it?
answer_data: Retraction reference with the retracting agent
Supersession pointer to the replacement item
Rule that the retracted item is marked and retained, never deleted in place

questions.text: What evidence was expected but missing, and how is a deliberate absence distinguished from a silent gap?
answer_data: Declared absent-evidence note with the reason
Distinction between not sought, sought and unavailable, and withheld under policy
Effect of the declared absence on the recorded confidence

data_elements.name: Evidence as-of instant
data_elements.description: Instant the evidence item speaks to, distinct from when it was cited.

data_elements.name: Freshness window
data_elements.description: Duration beyond which the item should not be relied on without re-checking.

data_elements.name: Retraction reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a correction, supersession or withdrawal issued by the evidence owner.

data_elements.name: Absent-evidence note
data_elements.description: Declaration of evidence that was expected but not obtained, with the reason and its effect on confidence.

data_elements.name: Revalidation due point
data_elements.description: Point at which the assertion is scheduled for evidence revalidation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Freshness, retraction and absence are temporal and status attributes of evidence items whose content already lives in the retained exhibit artifact. Holding a separate document would split one item's status from its content and invite the two to disagree.

layers.name: Review, disagreement and undetermined state
layers.description: How human judgement is recorded, how competing assertions from different authorities coexist, and how the model refuses to invent a winner.

findings.name: Human review, adjudication outcome and reason
findings.description: Clerical review is a defined part of linkage, not an afterthought, and reviewer sign-off is what separates a tool proposal from a curated assertion. This finding records why a pair reached review at all (a possible-link band, a random quality sample, an external challenge), who reviewed it and whether they were independent of the asserter, what outcome they reached (confirmed, rejected, amended or deferred) and the reason given. A deferred outcome is preserved rather than converted into a rejection.

questions.text: Why did this pair enter human review rather than being accepted or rejected automatically?
answer_data: Review trigger code covering possible-link band, quality sample, escalation and external challenge
Reference to the sampling or escalation rule applied
Volume context showing what proportion of comparable pairs were reviewed

questions.text: What outcome did the reviewer reach, and what reason was recorded for it?
answer_data: Outcome code covering confirmed, rejected, amended and deferred
Free-text or coded reason
Amended predicate or amended confidence where the outcome changed the assertion

questions.text: When did the review occur and what activity record ties the outcome to the reviewer?
answer_data: Review instant in RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z
Reference to the review activity and its qualified association with the reviewer
Adjudication record reference

questions.text: Was the reviewer independent of the asserter, and who owns the adjudication outcome once recorded?
answer_data: Independence flag comparing reviewer against asserter and approver
Owning authority for the adjudication outcome
Statement that the outcome is content of this model while any proof-of-access log belongs to the referenced audit model

data_elements.name: Review activity reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the review activity and its association with the reviewing agent.

data_elements.name: Adjudication outcome
data_elements.description: Outcome reached by the reviewer: confirmed, rejected, amended or deferred.

data_elements.name: Adjudication reason
data_elements.description: Recorded reason supporting the adjudication outcome.

data_elements.name: Review trigger
data_elements.description: Basis on which the pair was routed to human review.

data_elements.name: Reviewer independence flag
data_elements.description: Whether the reviewer is distinct from the asserter and the approving actor.

artifacts.name: Adjudication record
artifacts.description: The durable record of one review decision on one assertion: reviewer, trigger, evidence consulted, outcome, reason and any amendment made, retained so the decision can be re-examined by a later reviewer or an external challenger.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Case identifier issued by the adjudicating authority's review system where one exists; otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, scoped to the assertion identifier with a monotonically increasing review sequence number and no date component.

findings.name: Competing assertions, confidence revision and the undetermined state
findings.description: Two authorities can assert incompatible things about the same pair, and a probabilistic method can land in a band where no decision is warranted. The model represents disagreement as a state over a set of coexisting assertions rather than as a single mutated record: each competing assertion keeps its own asserter, authority, method and evidence; a confidence revision adds a new statement and marks the prior one superseded rather than overwriting it; and undetermined is a first-class terminal-for-now state distinct from rejected and from unassessed. Selection of an operative assertion, where a consumer needs one, is a downstream decision recorded with its own attribution, not an inference this model performs.

questions.text: How are two incompatible assertions about the same pair held together without either being discarded?
answer_data: References to each competing assertion with its own attribution and method
Disagreement state code covering agreed, disputed and undetermined
Rule prohibiting deletion or in-place edit of a competing assertion

questions.text: When confidence changes, how is the prior confidence statement preserved rather than overwritten?
answer_data: New confidence statement with its own decision instant and method reference
Supersession pointer from the new statement to the prior one
Immutability rule for superseded statements

questions.text: What does an undetermined state assert, and how does it differ from rejected and from never assessed?
answer_data: Undetermined state definition with the recorded reason for no decision
Distinction from asserted non-identity and from an unassessed pair
Conditions under which the state may be revisited

questions.text: Who selects an operative assertion for downstream use, and how is that selection kept out of the evidence record?
answer_data: Reference to the consuming system or policy model that performs selection
Attribution of the selection decision to its own actor and instant
Statement that this model records but never performs the selection

questions.text: How is a disputed or undetermined pair exported to a vocabulary that has no way to express disagreement?
answer_data: Export rule suppressing disputed pairs from transitive or substitution-licensing predicates
Downgrade rule to a non-transitive close-match style predicate where suppression is not acceptable
Warning annotation carried alongside the exported statement

data_elements.name: Competing assertion reference
data_elements.description: Reference to another assertion about the same pair that conflicts with this one.

data_elements.name: Disagreement state
data_elements.description: State over the set of assertions about a pair: agreed, disputed or undetermined.

data_elements.name: Confidence revision reference
data_elements.description: Pointer from a new confidence statement to the prior statement it supersedes, which remains immutable.

data_elements.name: Supersession reference
data_elements.description: Pointer recording that this assertion has been superseded by a later one, without removal.

data_elements.name: No-decision reason
data_elements.description: Recorded reason why no equivalence decision was reached for this pair.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Disagreement is a computed relationship over assertion records that already exist, expressed as state codes and cross-references. Materialising a dispute document would create a fourth account of the pair competing with the assertions it summarises, and would need its own reconciliation the moment any member assertion changed.

functions.name: Record assertion provenance envelope
functions.description: Capture the attributable envelope around one equivalence assertion: the distinct actor roles, the source-system and master-record bindings, the derivation lineage and the separately recorded time points.
inputs: Source-system and master-record references per side
Decision, observation, ingestion and creation instants
outputs: Provenance envelope bound to the assertion
preconditions: Both identifiers resolve within declared namespaces
The asserter reference resolves in the external party registry
All supplied instants conform to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
effects: Assertion becomes attributable and its lineage traversable
Missing roles are recorded as explicitly absent rather than left ambiguous

functions.name: Register a confidence statement reported by a referenced method
functions.description: Record a score, its scale, the thresholds in force, the resulting decision region and any explanation, as an outcome reported by an external method. This function stores and validates a reported measurement; it never computes, re-scores or optimises one.
inputs: Method reference with tool version and configuration digest
outputs: Confidence statement attached to the assertion
preconditions: The referenced method and its configuration digest are recorded
The score scale is declared and its bounds known
effects: Confidence becomes queryable independently of relation semantics and authority
A score on an undeclared or incompatible scale is refused rather than coerced

functions.name: Attach, supersede or retract an evidence item
functions.description: Register a discrete evidence item against an assertion with polarity, citation, digest, strength, sensitivity classification and jurisdiction of origin, or mark an existing item retracted or superseded without removing it.
inputs: Evidence item reference or retained exhibit
Polarity, strength, sensitivity and jurisdiction values
Retraction or supersession pointer where applicable
outputs: Evidence item registered against the assertion
Updated evidence status without loss of the prior item
preconditions: The item has a resolvable citation or a content digest
Retraction supplies the retracting agent and instant
effects: Supporting and refuting evidence coexist under the same assertion
Retracted items remain inspectable, marked rather than deleted

functions.name: Record a human review and adjudication outcome
functions.description: Record why a pair reached review, who reviewed it, whether they were independent, the outcome reached and the reason, together with any amendment made to the predicate or confidence.
inputs: Reviewer agent reference and independence flag
Outcome code, reason and any amendment
outputs: Adjudication record bound to the assertion
Amended predicate or confidence statement where the outcome changed the assertion
preconditions: The assertion exists and its current state is readable by the reviewer
The reviewer agent resolves in the external party registry
Review instant conforms to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
effects: The assertion is distinguishable as human-confirmed rather than tool-proposed
A deferred outcome is preserved and does not become a rejection

functions.name: Raise a disagreement and set the undetermined state
functions.description: Record that two or more assertions about the same pair conflict, or that a method returned no warranted decision, and place the pair in a disputed or undetermined state without selecting a winner or mutating any member assertion.
inputs: References to the conflicting assertions or the undecided pair
Reason for no decision or for the conflict
outputs: Disagreement state over the assertion set
No-decision reason attached to the pair
preconditions: Each member assertion carries its own attribution and method reference
No prior evidence or confidence statement is modified by this call
effects: Competing assertions coexist with independent provenance
Selection of an operative assertion is deferred to the consuming system and attributed there

functions.name: Check an assertion against a declared evidence and provenance profile
functions.description: Report whether an assertion satisfies a declared minimum profile: required actor roles present, method identity and configuration digest recorded, score scale declared, evidence polarity coverage met, and time points conforming. The function reports conformance only; consequences of non-conformance are decided by the adopting Dimension's policy model.
outputs: Conformance report listing satisfied and unsatisfied requirements
preconditions: A profile has been declared and versioned
The assertion record is readable at the requested scope
effects: Gaps in evidence and provenance become visible and comparable across assertions
No blocking, refusal or enforcement occurs within this model

functions.name: Project the evidence and confidence record into an alignment target
functions.description: Serialise the assertion's provenance, method, confidence and evidence into an external interchange form, applying the declared projection constraints so that a disputed, undetermined or low-strength assertion is not silently promoted into a transitive or substitution-licensing predicate.
outputs: Interchange representation in the target vocabulary
Suppression and downgrade log listing what was withheld or weakened and why
preconditions: Relation predicate and semantic strength are recorded
Disagreement state is resolved to agreed, or an explicit downgrade rule is supplied
Namespace expansion map is available for both sides
effects: Exported statements carry method, confidence and review provenance rather than a bare link
Assertions ineligible for transitive closure are withheld or downgraded, never exported as exact equivalence by default

composition.purpose: Inherit what an identifier is, who issues it, its namespace and its validity rules. This model adds only the assertion that two such identifiers denote the same subject, plus the evidence, provenance and confidence qualifying that assertion; it does not mint, format or re-validate identifiers.

composition.target: Agent and party registry of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Resolve asserter, authority, publisher, reviewer and approver references to typed agents. This model carries the role binding and the mandate citation for each assertion; agent identity, agent lifecycle and organisational hierarchy remain owned by the registry.

composition.target: Entity-resolution and matching engine (external runtime component)
composition.purpose: Carry the method reference, tool version, configuration digest, feature inventory, thresholds and reported score as recorded parameters and outcomes. Execution, scheduling, blocking, scoring and threshold optimisation stay with the engine; holding a score confers no ownership of the scoring process.

composition.target: W3C PROV-O and PROV-DM provenance vocabularies
composition.purpose: Bind local roles and lineage to prov:wasAttributedTo, qualified association and role, prov:wasDerivedFrom, prov:hadPrimarySource, prov:wasRevisionOf and prov:Bundle. Alignment is claimed at the binding level only; no conformance claim is made without a validated profile.

composition.target: SSSOM Mapping and MappingSet metadata model
composition.purpose: Map local method, justification, author, creator, reviewer, tool version, source version, confidence and predicate-modifier fields onto their SSSOM counterparts for interchange of mapping sets, without adopting SSSOM's file-format or propagation rules as internal semantics.

composition.target: SKOS mapping properties and OWL 2 individual (in)equality axioms
composition.purpose: Reference exactMatch, closeMatch, SameIndividual and DifferentIndividuals as the governed predicates whose transitivity, symmetry, disjointness and substitution licensing are defined externally. This model records which predicate is asserted and constrains export onto it; it never restates or varies their entailment rules.

composition.target: W3C Data Quality Vocabulary measurement model
composition.purpose: Express calibration and evaluation results as quality measurements against named metrics and dimensions, with PROV supplying the provenance of the assessment. Metric catalogues and the running of assessments remain outside this model.

composition.target: Evaluation dataset and gold-standard corpus registry
composition.purpose: Point at the reference data against which linkage quality was measured, with its representativeness caveat. Curation, governance and access control of that corpus, including any restriction on its reuse, are owned by the registry.

composition.target: Access-control, consent and retention policy model of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Supply the sensitivity classification, jurisdiction of origin and access classification that a policy model needs as inputs. Evaluation of those policies, enforcement of access decisions and execution of disposition and deletion occur entirely in that model.

composition.target: Audit and event-log model of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Cite audit records that evidence who read, asserted or adjudicated an equivalence. Audit-trail semantics, immutability guarantees and log retention are owned by that model; this model stores only the reference.

composition.target: Subject models requiring federated identity equivalence
composition.purpose: Attach the alias assertion surface, with its evidence, provenance and confidence qualifiers, to any subject model whose instances are known under identifiers in more than one system, without that model redefining equivalence semantics locally.

Take the graded-evidence and identity-resolution concepts as an external reference frame for authority-derived assurance. Identity proofing processes, credential service provider obligations and assurance-level determination are performed under that guidance, not by this model.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names a single accountable owner for the alias-assertion package, distinct from the owner of any referenced matching engine or policy model, and records that owner as a resolvable agent reference.

The owner publishes the governed vocabularies the package depends on: relation predicates with their transitivity and substitution properties, mapping-justification categories, score scales with bounds, evidence strength grades, sensitivity classifications and disagreement states.
The owner declares at least one versioned evidence-and-provenance profile stating the minimum required elements for an assertion to be publishable, and versions it independently of the schema.
The owner declares the namespace expansion map for every identifier namespace appearing on either side of an assertion, so that exported assertions are unambiguous outside the originating store.
The owner records which referenced models own evaluation, enforcement, audit-trail storage and deletion execution, so that no consumer mistakes a reference held here for local ownership.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local identifiers are scoped to the adopting Dimension and carry no meaning outside it. Every external identifier appearing as a subject or object is stored with an explicit namespace or prefix declaration and is never abbreviated without one, because the same short form can expand differently in two source systems. Namespace declarations are versioned alongside source versions, and a namespace whose expansion changes is treated as a new namespace rather than an in-place edit. Method, tool, agent and evidence references use the identifier issued by their owning system, expanded through the same declared map.
registry_links: Registry record vr.wm-xct-036 in the world-model record plane, with review state boundary-review-required
Navigation path NAV.XCT.ALS and domain tag XCT.ALS
Parent registry entry WM-XCT-011, which supplies identifier semantics this model does not redefine
Governed relation-predicate vocabulary maintained by the adopting Dimension and aligned to SKOS and OWL 2
Method and tool registry supplying method references, tool versions and configuration digests

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is the format-neutral assertion record: subject reference, object reference, relation predicate, semantic strength, provenance envelope, method reference, confidence statements, evidence items and state. JSON, YAML, Markdown, RDF, Git objects and document stores are projections of this form and none is authoritative over it.

Identifiers are canonicalised by expanding every prefix through the declared namespace map before comparison; two assertions are the same assertion only when both expanded sides, the predicate and the asserting agent match.
All instants are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; a value lacking seconds or an offset is rejected at ingestion rather than normalised by assumption.

Score values are canonicalised only within a declared scale; values on different scales are never coerced onto a common scale, because no validated crosswalk exists between bounded probabilities, unbounded likelihood weights and ordinal assurance levels.
Ordered structures that affect reproduction, notably normalization step sequences and blocking pass order, preserve their order under canonicalisation.
patch_rules: Confidence, adjudication and evidence statements are append-only: a change is expressed as a new statement carrying its own agent, instant and method reference, with a supersession pointer to the statement it replaces. In-place mutation of a prior statement is prohibited.
Correcting a factual recording error, such as a mistyped source reference, is a patch that must itself be attributed and must retain the prior value in the superseded record.
A patch may never alter the relation predicate, semantic strength or score of a published assertion; those changes create a new assertion that supersedes the old one.
Retracting an evidence item marks it retracted with the retracting agent and instant; the item and its digest remain readable so a past decision stays reconstructable.
Patches touching evidence classified as sensitive record the change reference only; the classification decision and any consequent restriction are resolved by the referenced policy model.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional data element, a new governed vocabulary term or a new evidence class is a minor change; consumers ignore unknown optional elements.

Narrowing a cardinality, making an element required, removing a vocabulary term or changing the meaning of a score scale is a breaking change requiring a new package version and a stated migration path.

Vocabularies version independently of the structure; an assertion records the vocabulary version in force at its decision instant so historical assertions remain interpretable after a term is deprecated.

Exported alignments to external vocabularies are advisory: a change in the aligned specification does not silently change the meaning of stored assertions, and no conformance is claimed without a validated profile and recorded test evidence.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier issued by the system of record that governs the referenced thing, used verbatim together with an explicit reference to its issuing system, for example an evidence document number issued by the issuing register or a review case identifier issued by the adjudicating authority's case system.

Governed global identifier or IRI: a persistent identifier from a governed scheme, such as a resolvable researcher or organisation identifier for agents, a DOI for an evaluation report, or a versioned method IRI from a method registry.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only when neither of the above exists, permanently bound to a content digest where the artifact has stable content, and never reissued.

A content digest may serve as the primary key for immutable artifacts such as configuration snapshots and evidence exhibits, but a digest is a verification value and does not replace a master-system identifier where one exists.
A date, a version label, a filename or a sequence position is never an identifier on its own and must not be used as one.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded as RFC 3339 date-time strings that include seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; values lacking seconds or an offset are rejected at ingestion rather than normalised by assumption. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately whenever they differ: the decision instant at which the equivalence was determined, the observation instant at which each compared source state was read, the ingestion instant at which the assertion entered this store and the record creation instant are distinct elements, and none is substituted for another. Evidence carries its own as-of instant distinct from its citation instant. Where a UTC instant is known but the local offset is not, the -00:00 offset form is used rather than Z, so that an unknown offset is not mistaken for a UTC preference.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, namely configuration snapshots, evaluation reports, evidence exhibits and adjudication records, are named by a stable scope prefix plus a monotonically increasing sequence number within that scope: configuration snapshots sequence within a method identifier, evaluation reports within a method and evaluation dataset pair, evidence exhibits within an assertion, and adjudication records within an assertion. Sequence numbers are never reused after supersession or retraction, and no date component appears in the name, because a date does not identify and collides under re-runs.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every retained artifact carries a content digest with its algorithm named, recorded at the moment of retention. Configuration snapshots and evidence exhibits are immutable once digested; a correction produces a new serial instance that references the prior one rather than replacing it. Digests are verified before an artifact is relied on to reproduce a decision, and a digest mismatch places the dependent assertion into the undetermined state pending review rather than silently invalidating it. Where an evidence item may not be retained, a digest stub is kept so the absence is provable and the original remains identifiable.

policies: Confidence, formal relation semantics and authority are three independent axes and are stored in separate elements. No process may derive one from another: a high score never sets the semantic strength, an authoritative assertion never implies an error estimate, and an assurance level never substitutes for a score.

Evidence and confidence statements are append-only and attributable. No process may overwrite, silently reconcile or delete a prior statement in order to present a single clean answer; disagreement is represented, not resolved by erasure.

An assertion in a disputed or undetermined state is never exported by default onto a transitive or substitution-licensing predicate; it is withheld or explicitly downgraded to a non-transitive predicate, and the suppression is logged in the export result.

Locally invented matching rules are labelled as local heuristics and are never presented as a governed standard method; an assertion produced by an unlabelled or unrecorded method may not be published under a declared evidence profile.

Sensitivity classification and jurisdiction of origin are recorded for every evidence item as inputs to the referenced policy model. This model performs no access evaluation and no enforcement, and no local field may be interpreted as an authorisation decision.

Reproducibility is a publication precondition for automated assertions: the method reference, tool version, configuration digest, feature inventory, thresholds and score scale must all be present, or the assertion is marked non-conformant to the declared profile.

read: Read an assertion with its full provenance envelope, method reference, confidence statements, evidence items and current state, resolved through the declared namespace map.
Read a redacted projection that exposes evidence polarity, strength and count without item content, for consumers not cleared to read sensitive evidence.
Read the history of confidence statements and adjudication outcomes for one assertion, including superseded and retracted entries, in decision-instant order.
Read all assertions produced by a given method reference and configuration digest, to scope the impact of a discovered method defect.
Read the set of competing assertions for a pair together with the disagreement state and no-decision reason, without any implied ranking.
create: Create an assertion with its subject and object references, relation predicate, semantic strength and provenance envelope; the asserter reference, agent kind, origin mode, decision instant and record creation instant are mandatory at creation.
Create a confidence statement bound to an existing assertion and to a recorded method reference, tool version and configuration digest, with the score scale declared.
Create an evidence item with polarity, citation or digest, strength, sensitivity classification and jurisdiction of origin, and optionally a retained exhibit.
Create an adjudication record capturing trigger, reviewer, independence flag, outcome and reason.
Create a disagreement or undetermined state over an existing set of assertions, with the recorded reason and the raising agent.
update: Update is append-and-supersede: a new statement is created with its own agent and instant and a supersession pointer; the superseded statement remains readable and immutable.

Correcting a recording error, such as a mistyped source or namespace reference, is permitted as an attributed patch that retains the prior value; it may never change a predicate, semantic strength or score.
Marking an evidence item retracted or superseded updates its status only; the item, its digest and its prior status remain readable.
Amending an assertion following adjudication creates a new assertion that supersedes the prior one and cites the adjudication record; the prior assertion is not edited.
Vocabulary term deprecation updates the vocabulary, never the historical assertions that used the term; those retain the vocabulary version in force at their decision instant.
delete: Default disposition is tombstone, not removal: an assertion, confidence statement, evidence item or adjudication record that is withdrawn is marked withdrawn with the withdrawing agent, instant and reason, and its identifier, digests and supersession pointers are retained so that past decisions and exports stay reconstructable and dangling references remain resolvable.

Hard erasure is performed only on instruction from the adopting Dimension's retention, consent and disposition policy model, which owns the legal basis, the retention schedule and the execution of deletion; this model neither evaluates nor enforces that policy and never initiates erasure on its own authority.
